title: I Give You My Silence by Mario Vargas Llosa review – Nobel laureate’s final novel is a love letter to Peru

paragraphs.en: When I Give You My Silence was published in Spanish in 2023 its author, the Peruvian Nobel laureate Mario Vargas Llosa, rightly predicted that it would be his final novel. He died last year at the age of 89. I Give You My Silence may have been completed with the spectre of death approaching, but there is nothing morbid about this book, which is an eccentric love letter to Vargas Llosa’s native country and, in particular, its music.
paragraphs.zh: 当《我把我的沉默献给你》于 2023 年以西班牙语出版时，它的作者、秘鲁诺贝尔文学奖得主马里奥·巴尔加斯·略萨正确地预言这将是他的最后一部长篇小说。他于去年去世，享年 89 岁。《我把我的沉默献给你》或许是在死亡逼近的阴影下完成的，但这本书没有丝毫阴郁之气，它是一封写给巴尔加斯·略萨祖国、尤其是其音乐的一封别具一格的情书。

paragraphs.en: The novel’s quixotic hero is a music journalist called Toño Azpilcueta. Toño always hoped to be a professor of Peruvian music, but as the novel opens, he’s earning a meagre living teaching at a girls’ school and writing articles for specialist magazines. Luckily, he’s subsidised by his longsuffering wife, Matilde. Toño is a recognisable type: the impecunious cultural obsessive. If he were British, he would be fanatical about free jazz, or some obscure Delta bluesman. But this is Peru and Toño’s particular infatuation is the vals , a Peruvian musical style that fuses the European waltz with African and indigenous Latin American traditions.
paragraphs.zh: 小说那位堂吉诃德式的男主角是一位名叫托尼奥·阿斯皮尔库埃塔的音乐记者。托尼奥一直希望成为秘鲁音乐的教授，但在小说开头，他靠在一所女子学校教书和为专业杂志撰稿勉强糊口。幸运的是，他得到了长期忍气吞声的妻子玛蒂尔德的经济支持。托尼奥是一种令人熟悉的人物类型：囊中羞涩的文化痴迷者。如果他是英国人，他会狂热地痴迷于自由爵士，或者某个冷门的三角洲布鲁斯乐手。但这里是秘鲁，托尼奥特别痴迷的是“vals”这种秘鲁音乐风格，它融合了欧洲华尔兹与非洲及拉丁美洲原住民传统。

paragraphs.en: One evening, Toño gets an invitation to see an unknown guitarist called Lalo Molfino, who blows him away with his incredible virtuosity. Before Toño has time to digest the musician’s brilliance, he learns of his sudden death. With the help of a small gift of money from a friend, Toño embarks on a project to write a biography of Molfino. “This book would be an homage to his talent, but also much more: he would at last put to paper those ideas about the Peruvian vals he had entertained so often.”
paragraphs.zh: 一天晚上，托尼奥收到邀请去看一位名叫拉洛·莫尔菲诺的不知名吉他手演出，后者令人难以置信的演奏技巧让他大为倾倒。托尼奥还没来得及消化这位音乐家的才华，就得知了他的猝然离世。在一位朋友的一小笔资助下，托尼奥开启了一个项目：为莫尔菲诺写传记。“这本书将是对他才华的致敬，但意义远不止于此：他终将把那些关于秘鲁 vals 的、他思考过无数次的想法付诸笔端。”

paragraphs.en: Toño’s Big Idea is that the vals is going to save Peru, and possibly humanity. Its blended heritage, he explains, points a way past the trauma that colonialism, racism, dictatorship and terrorism have inflicted on his country. Toño’s quest to write the book involves sleuthing, research, interviews, a journey along Peru’s Pacific coast to Molfino’s birthplace, and battles with his own demons – in particular, a phobia about rats.
paragraphs.zh: 托尼奥的“大构想”是：vals 将拯救秘鲁，甚至可能拯救全人类。他解释说，它融合性的传承为走出殖民主义、种族主义、独裁统治和恐怖主义给这个国家带来的创伤指明了一条道路。托尼奥的写书之旅包括调查、研究、访谈、沿着秘鲁太平洋海岸前往莫尔菲诺的出生地，以及与自己内心恶魔的搏斗——尤其是对老鼠的恐惧症。

paragraphs.en: Coming to this book with, I think, the median British knowledge of Peru (Machu Picchu, the Shining Path, ceviche, Paddington Bear), it took me a moment to orient myself. I knew nothing about the country’s music and I didn’t realise that Cecilia Barraza, an important recurring character, is a real-life Peruvian singer. (It’s a bit like having Patti Smith turn up in a novel.) Nor did I clock to begin with that the novel is really two books in one. The odd-numbered chapters are a third-person account of Toño’s attempt to research and write the biography. Most of the even-numbered chapters are excerpts from the final work, I Give You My Silence. These end up forming a quirky primer on Peruvian music and culture. It includes essays on the history of the vals ; the lives of the musicians who created it; the cajon , a distinctive Peruvian percussion instrument; Spanish as a regional lingua franca; and huachafería , a concept that Toño sees as a key part of Peru’s identity . Huach afería holds huge significance for both Toño and Vargas Llosa. The novel’s translator, Adrian Nathan West, tells us in a helpful afterword that “dictionaries typically define it as pretension”. Toño is much more effusive: “ Huachafería can be brilliant, but it is rarely intelligent: it is intuitive, verbose, solemn, melodic, imaginative and above all maudlin.”
paragraphs.zh: 带着——我想——英国人对秘鲁的中等水平了解（马丘比丘、光辉道路、酸橘汁腌鱼、帕丁顿熊）来读这本书，我花了一会儿才找准方向。我对这个国家的音乐一无所知，也没意识到塞西莉亚·巴拉萨这个重要的反复出现的角色，其实是现实中的秘鲁歌手（这有点像帕蒂·史密斯出现在小说里）。我一开始也没意识到，这部小说其实是两本书合二为一。奇数章节以第三人称叙述托尼奥研究和撰写传记的过程；大多数偶数章节则是最终作品《我把我的沉默献给你》的片段。这些片段最终构成了一本别具一格的秘鲁音乐与文化入门读物，其中包括关于 vals 的历史、创作它的音乐家们的人生、秘鲁特色打击乐器 cajon（木箱鼓）、西班牙语作为地区通用语言，以及 huachafería 这一托尼奥视为秘鲁身份认同关键部分的概念的随笔。huachafería 对托尼奥和巴尔加斯·略萨都意义重大。小说的译者阿德里安·内森·韦斯特在翔实的后记中告诉我们，“词典通常把它定义为‘矫揉造作’”。托尼奥则要热情得多：“huachafería 可能才华横溢，但很少是明智的：它直觉、冗长、庄严、悦耳、富有想象力，最重要的是多愁善感。”

paragraphs.en: Gentle, impractical dreamers, Vargas Llosa seems to be saying, bring their own kind of changes into the world
paragraphs.zh: 温柔而不切实际的梦想家，巴尔加斯·略萨似乎在说，会以自己的方式给世界带来改变。

paragraphs.en: This is, in fact, a perfect description of the book that Toño himself is writing, which includes the grandiose and impossible claim that “this book you hold in your hands, reader, will be the starting point of a true revolution that will pull our Peru up from poverty and sorrow, restoring its glory and its creativity, making it a place where all are truly equal and putting an end to the sad divisions of its people”.
paragraphs.zh: 事实上，这恰恰是对托尼奥自己正在写的那本书的完美描述，书中包含一个宏大而不切实际的宣言：“读者，你捧在手中的这本书，将是一场真正革命的起点，它将把我们的秘鲁从贫困和悲伤中拉出来，恢复它的荣光与创造力，使它成为一个人人真正平等的地方，终结它的人民可悲的分裂。”

paragraphs.en: Toño’s mission is clearly bonkers, but he approaches it with a heroic single-mindedness that wins the reader over. And the form the novel takes allows Vargas Llosa to have his cake and eat it too: giving Toño space to explore his ideas in detail, while simultaneously having fun pointing out how overheated they are.
paragraphs.zh: 托尼奥的使命显然疯狂，但他以一种征服读者的英雄式专注对待它。而小说采用的形式让巴尔加斯·略萨可以两全其美：给托尼奥空间去详细探讨他的想法，同时又兴味盎然地指出这些想法有多么过热。
